description: Less than a year after the tragic passing of her son, Malcolm-Jamal Warner, Pam Warner takes the TEDxManhattanBeach stage with extraordinary grace and courage. In a deeply moving tribute, she honors Malcolm’s legacy and the message he championed: that vulnerability is not weakness, but strength. Reflecting on his commitment to authenticity, intentional living, and radical self-acceptance, Pam invites us to carry his light forward. Following her introduction, Malcolm’s powerful 2023 TEDxManhattanBeach talk, “Vulnerability Is My Superpower,” is shared with the audience—reminding us all to live bravely, truthfully, and open-heartedly. Pam Warner is the devoted mother of the late actor, musician, and cultural figure Malcolm-Jamal Warner, best known for his Emmy-nominated role as Theo Huxtable on The Cosby Show. title: Remembering Malcolm Jamal-Warner through his Mother’s Eyes | Pam Warner | TEDxManhattanBeach

description:
Six months after the Palisades Fire displaced his family and hollowed out his neighborhood, Zacharie Sergenian discovers that grief doesn’t arrive with flames—it arrives in silence. In a quiet, powerful moment when music finally returns to his empty home, he reflects on how sound signals life, community, and healing after disaster. This talk is a moving meditation on delayed loss, resilience, and the small human moments that help us find our way back home. #fire #Palisadesfire #firestorm #LAfires Zacharie Sergenian is a Los Angeles high school student who has found his voice through storytelling. Six months after the Pacific Palisades Fire devastated his neighborhood and school, he worked with USC’s Wildfire Youth Media Initiative to create an audio piece exploring grief, delayed loss, and returning home after disaster—centered on the quiet act of having a friend play his piano.

Zacharie is a senior at Palisades Charter High School, where he remains active in student journalism while
title: After the LA fires, the sounds that felt like home | Zacharie Sergenian | TEDxManhattanBeach

author: TEDx Talks
description: Wenxin addresses why she still creates hand-drawn art in an AI-dominated age. She traces her artistic journey, from a random childhood drawing to rediscovering creativity via Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse and a praised campus art piece. She explores color as an emotional language, her club’s color-based diversity activity, and emphasizes human creativity and emotion are irreplaceable by AI—art is about expressing one’s true self. Melody is very interested in the art of visual storytelling, creativity, and the role of humanities in the age of AI. Through calligraphy, painting, and design, she explores how color and art can express identity and emotion. Melody is of the opinion that creativity is not the antithesis of technology, but is a vital force for us to retain the humanity in a quickly changing world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Painting My “I AM” in the Age of AI | Wenxin (Melody) Ke | TEDxWuxi Big Bridge Academy Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
La scienza è un atto di resistenza, appartiene a tutti e non è privilegio di pochi. Non serve solo per grandi scoperte, ma per affrontare problemi concreti, migliorare la vita delle persone e accendere curiosità. Con piccoli gesti quotidiani possiamo diffondere conoscenza, responsabilità e innovazione; condividere la scienza è resistere all’oscurità dell’ignoranza e creare un futuro migliore per tutti. Insegna Sistemi Automatici all’ITIS Enrico Fermi di Roma.
Attraverso il suo podcast “Pillole di Scienza” racconta la scienza con passione, trasformando formule e circuiti in storie che accendono curiosità e conoscenza anche fuori dall’aula.
Con i suoi studenti realizza prototipi innovativi:caschi intelligenti, robot per il riciclo, carrelli per anziani, nidi smart, dispositivi per la salute... trasformando teoria in esperienze concrete, e contribuendo a far crescere menti curiose.
Ha ricevuto riconoscimenti istituzionali ed è stato nominato tra i 50 migliori insegnanti al mondo dal Glob
title: La scienza è un atto di resistenza | Leonardo Durante | TEDxSpoleto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
La sicurezza sul lavoro non può essere "taglia unica". Le persone sono diverse, donne, uomini, corpi con disabilità. 
Per proteggerle davvero, bisogna guardare i dati, creare soluzioni concrete e non fermarsi mai. Rialzarsi dopo una caduta significa trasformare un problema in opportunità; la sicurezza è un atto d’amore, e fare la cosa giusta è responsabilità di tutti. Come comunicatrice e giornalista, ha anni di esperienza nel raccontare l’innovazione, non solo tecnologica. Il suo percorso internazionale nell’ingegneria e nell’energia l'ha portato a interrogarsi su due sfide decisive per il nostro tempo: sicurezza ed equità. Due dimensioni che sembrano distinte, ma che, nei dati e nella realtà quotidiana, rivelano connessioni sorprendenti. 
Come Chief Happiness Officer invita a guardare il lavoro con occhi nuovi, e come public speaking coach incoraggia a dire quella cosa diversa che tutti hanno in testa. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independe

He details the immense craftsmanship behind game creation, the unparalleled immersion games bring to players, and how they record era-specific culture and spirit—like Animal Crossing connecting people during the pandemic. He makes a compelling case for games as a meaningful, artistic medium. Echo is a high school student who serves as a subject representative, a member of the Student Union, and a school club president, and also a dedicated gamer with a penchant for delving into the artistic side of games. Having immersed herself in diverse game genres—from indie narrative gems to open-world epics—Echo has developed a thoughtful perspective on the artistic connotations of video games. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Robots are often portrayed as threats, machines that replace jobs, remove human value, or create distance between people and purpose. This panel challenges those assumptions by exploring what robotics truly is, how it works, and why it matters.
Through real projects and practical examples, the discussion reveals robotics as a creative, human-centered field that blends engineering, imagination, and responsibility. From assistive technologies designed for safety and accessibility to the role of artificial intelligence in decision-making, the panel reframes robots not as replacements for humans, but as tools that extend human capability.
Looking ahead, the conversation shifts from science fiction to reality. It asks how robotics can address gaps in healthcare, education, and safety, especially in contexts where resources are limited. The future of robotics, it suggests, is not about machines becoming human, but about humans choosing how technology serves society. Homayun Falak is an educ
title: Robots, Intelligence & Future | Homayun Falak, Nargis Qorbani & Yasamin Hussaini | TEDxShar e Naw

description:
In his TEDx talk, he speaks about the fragility of human existence, the oftenoverlooked influence of chance and fortunate circumstances that lead to undeserved success, and the importance of teachers constantly questioningthemselves.
Empathy and compassion may not guarantee our collective success as humanity—but they are certainly an important step toward it. Michael Liechti, is a 49-year-old high school teacher from the German-speaking part of Switzerland, and for nearly 25 years he has been teaching German and philosophy at various schools in the canton of Vaud.
His academic interests lie in modern literature, foreign language teaching, and philosophy as an interdisciplinary school subject. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

FOMO is all around us, whether it’s parties, vacations with friends or social gatherings. Yet we rarely hear about the FOMO that comes with career opportunities. My speech will focus on the overwhelming feeling every student has experienced at least once in their lives, the feeling of losing control. We are told our success depends on our GPA’s, endless test scores and countless extracurricular activities, whatever they may be. 
But that isn’t always the surest path to success.
Sometimes, its the relief of missing out that guides us there. Eva de Groot is a student at EHL Hospitality Business School, navigating the high expectations, constant opportunities, and pressure to excel that define life at a top-tier institution. Like many ambitious students, she has experienced the overwhelming belief that success requires doing everything at once—achieving perfect grades, building an impressive résumé, and never saying no.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Climate change is often discussed in numbers, graphs, and distant forecasts, but its consequences are already present in daily life. This talk examines how environmental degradation, polluted air, and shifting climate patterns are directly affecting public health, livelihoods, and the future of communities in Afghanistan.
It argues that climate change is not only a natural phenomenon but largely the result of human actions, from industrial emissions to neglect of the environment. The burden of this crisis, however, is not shared equally. Children, vulnerable families, and those with limited access to healthcare are paying the highest price.
Rather than treating climate change as an abstract global issue, this talk frames it as an urgent human crisis, one that threatens lives, futures, and generational well-being. It calls for responsibility, awareness, and action, reminding us that protecting the environment is inseparable from protecting ourselves. Abdulhadi Achakzai is a climate cha
title: When the Climate Turns Against Us | Abdulhadi Achakzai | TEDxShar e Naw

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world where conversations move fast and opinions move faster, we often underestimate the quiet power of our words. But what if every sentence we speak leaves an invisible imprint — on someone’s mind, heart, or future? In this deeply reflective and thought-provoking talk at TEDxBITJaipur, Jayshree Kirtane explores how language is not just communication — it is creation. Every word carries energy. It can build confidence or quietly break it. It can heal wounds or deepen them. It can shape identities, relationships, and even the direction of a life. Through relatable stories and real-life experiences, she reminds us that words are never “just words.” They become memories. They become beliefs. They become the inner voice someone carries long after the conversation ends. This talk is a powerful reminder to pause before we speak, to choose empathy over impulse, and to recognize the responsibility that comes with expression. description:
Taking control over our own futures and not letting circumstances or fear of change cause us to reject the future. I am a Grade 11 student at Newton’s Grove School. Over the past few years, as I’ve grown and gotten closer to the age where I needed to think seriously about what my future would look like, I found that a lot of discourse geared towards the future was one which was incredibly negative and almost nihilistic. I soon found that these ideas began to infect my own belief of what the future was going to look like, giving me a rather grim outlook on the next ten years.

Though this discourse isn’t completely invalid, by reflecting more on the past and our current circumstances, I realized just how often it is blown out of proportion, and just how much we have become anchored in negativity. As I've observed the world around us, I've also noticed a quiet trade-off nobody talks about: we're optimizing everything while accidentally optimizing the human parts that make life worth living. When I think about the future and what the world will look like in the next 10 years, I question how people growing up in the next generation will form a sense of identity in a world shaped by constant influence. “I build things and blow things up.”

That may sound chaotic, but it is actually the foundation of science, discovery, and teaching the next generation.

In this dynamic TEDxYouth talk, a science teacher unpacks why the sky is blue, the power of rods and cones, and what wavelengths and energy levels have to do with understanding the world around us. But this is not just about science. It is about why we learn in the first place.

Through history, philosophy, and experimentation, curiosity has driven problem-solving and progress. From choosing a major to retaking exams, from relearning chemistry while substitute teaching to becoming a “compassionate commander” in the classroom, this talk explores what it truly takes to succeed.

The secret is not genius. It is curiosity, resilience, and the willingness to stay a student forever. Jon Bennett has been teaching at Crean Lutheran High School for over 10 years writing around 15 different high school math, science, and engineering courses. H

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does it really mean to become a physician? Is it a degree, a white coat, or something far more meaningful?

In this deeply personal talk, one doctor traces her medical calling back to 1870s England, where her great-grandmother worked as a scullery maid before becoming a midwife. Through two world wars, the influenza pandemic, thyroid storms treated with early surgical techniques, and an unexpected Ukrainian American love story, medicine became more than a profession—it became a family inheritance shaped by resilience, sacrifice, and service.

From house calls in London and Surrey to modern family practice in America, this story spans generations and continents. Yet the lesson remains strikingly simple and urgently relevant for today’s youth: The foundation of medicine is not technology, prestige, or achievement. It is listening.

Because every person matters. Dr. Duke is a recently retired board certified family medicine doctor. She has practiced medicine at Providence St. Jude M
title: The Making of a Physician: A Legacy of Listening | Alexandra Duke | TEDxCrean Lutheran HS Youth

Sibel Karataş, 1979 yılında Mersin’de doğmuştur. Yaşamı boyunca bu kentin insanına, kültürüne ve gelişimine katkı sunmayı temel bir sorumluluk olarak benimsemiştir. Atatürk Üniversitesi Filoloji Bölümü mezunudur. Uzun yıllar otel yöneticiliği yaptıktan sonra, doğa ve estetik tutkusunun izinden giderek Mersin’in ilk özel konsept çiçek mağazası olan Flower Concept’i kurmuştur.

description: Firstborns are often praised for being responsible—but what if that responsibility was learned under pressure, not chosen? This talk unpacks how birth order, culture, and family expectations quietly shape identity, emotional labor, and mental health. Being the first draft doesn’t mean you’re unfinished—it means you get to revise. Diya Pillai is a junior at Walton High School. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Thomas Locke explores how legal innovation has expanded the boundaries of patent law — and the unintended consequences that followed.

Who should be liable when a medicine is dispensed for a patented use — the manufacturer, the pharmacist, or no one at all? Thomas Locke is fascinated by the crossroads of law and medicine. A future trainee solicitor at Burges Salmon LLP, he studied History at Durham University before pursuing an MA in Law at the University of Law. He studies how existing medicines can be patented for new uses, uncovering the tension between rewarding discovery and ensuring patients get access to care. As host of the Johns Hopkins Malaria Minute podcast, Thomas translates scientific discovery into stories that inform and inspire. At TEDx, he asks: how can the law reward medical innovation without standing in the way of patients and the people who care for them?
